overall: Tomorrow (June 20, Juneteenth) is expected to see a significant recovery from today's storm-suppressed conditions, with partly sunny skies developing after overnight squall lines clear the Atlanta area. A lingering Flood Watch runs through 2am Friday, but daytime conditions should improve considerably with only a 30% chance of afternoon thunderstorms after 2pm and west winds around 10 mph. The NWS officially forecasts a high near 85°F after today's unusually cool observed high of 71.6°F caused by heavy rain and cloud cover.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is notably poor, with a ~5-6°F spread between two camps: ECMWF (~81.6°F), GFS (~80.7°F), and HRRR (~81.5°F) cluster in the low-80s, while NBM (~86.6°F) and Weather.com (~86.3°F) both point to the mid-to-upper 80s — a divergence that likely reflects disagreement over how quickly cloud cover scours out and how much daytime heating occurs post-frontal passage. The NWS text at 85°F aligns more closely with NBM, suggesting the dynamical models may be anchored low by today's cold prior-day observation (71.6°F).
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble model yields an expected TMAX of ~80.5°F, but this is almost certainly being pulled downward by the anomalously cold prior-day observation from today's heavy storms; the forecast-only model (81.2°F) similarly runs cool. The NWS text forecast of 85°F and NBM's 86.6°F are more consistent with seasonal norms for post-frontal clearing in Atlanta in late June. Both prediction tiers are rated Tier 4 (AVOID) with high entropy (2.77/2.75) and low peak bucket probabilities (~9%), reflecting genuine model uncertainty — the most probable range is 78–87°F, and confidence is low. Best estimate is approximately 83°F, splitting the gap between the dynamical model cluster and the NWS/NBM guidance.
